content: QUIC uses TLS 1.3 and RFC 9001 requires the client to authenticate server identity, normally by checking that the certificate contains the expected identity and chains to a trusted entity. Direct IP and hostname use must therefore compare the entered identity against certificate SANs or an explicitly provisioned certificate or public-key pin; mismatches must hard-fail. Test certificates, trust-all callbacks, and default credentials cannot be fallback paths. Sources: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9001.html and current service identity guidance https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9525.html.
